name: Victorian dress
blurb: High collars, bustles, crinolines and leg-of-mutton sleeves in costume and cosplay
title: Victorian Dress: Bustle, Sleeves & Costume Drawing Reference
description: Victorian-style dress reference: crinoline, bustle and leg-of-mutton silhouettes, high collars, how to draw them and how to wear the look in cosplay.
answer: A Victorian dress is women's clothing from, or inspired by, the reign of Queen Victoria (1837 to 1901). Its best-known features are a tightly fitted bodice, a long full skirt shaped by a crinoline or bustle, high collars for daywear and, in the 1890s, puffed leg-of-mutton sleeves. In Chinese and Japanese fandom, this kind of Western-style dress is often tagged 洋装 (Western dress).

sections.h: What a Victorian dress looks like
body: Victorian fashion changed a lot over six decades, which is useful for designers: pick one phase and the outfit becomes more convincing. The waist was always defined by a corset, the skirt always reached the floor for adults, and day dresses covered the neck and arms, while evening dresses could have lower necklines and short sleeves.
In fiction, the style suggests old money, mystery, gothic romance or steampunk adventure, and it is the main inspiration behind classic and gothic Lolita fashion.

body: Accessories that help the read: lace collars and cuffs, cameo brooches, gloves, bonnets or small tilted hats, parasols and buttoned boots.

sections.h: How to draw a Victorian dress

ul: Fix the waist first. It is narrow and slightly pointed at the front, and everything else is measured from it.
For a bustle, push the volume out behind the hips like a shelf, with drapery cascading down from it. The side view shows it best.
Leg-of-mutton sleeves are wide and puffed at the shoulder and tight from elbow to wrist; draw the puff as a rounded balloon with radiating gathers.
High collars wrap the neck in a short cylinder, often trimmed with lace at the top edge.
Use many horizontal trims, such as ruffles, pleated bands and lace rows, on the skirt; they wrap around the skirt as curved lines, not straight ones.

body: Cosplayers rarely need historical accuracy; a fitted bodice, a full floor-length skirt and one era-specific detail (bustle pad, big sleeves or high collar) is enough. A petticoat or small bustle pad gives the shape without full historical underpinnings.

Pose with an upright back and small, controlled gestures: hands folded at the waist, holding a parasol or fan, or turning in profile to show a bustle. Interiors with wood panelling, staircases, gardens or old brick streets suit the style, and warm, low light adds atmosphere.

faq.a: A bustle is a pad or frame worn at the back below the waist to push the skirt out behind. It was fashionable in the 1870s and 1880s.
Sleeves that are very full at the shoulder and narrow from the elbow down, shaped a little like a leg of lamb. They peaked in the mid-1890s.

faq.q: What does 洋装 mean in cosplay tags?
faq.a: It means Western-style dress and is used for European-inspired dresses, often Victorian or Rococo in feel, in contrast to traditional Chinese or Japanese clothing.
